clue.text: Sentimental garden-girl demands nothing in return

parts.note: Tennyson's poem begins 'Come into the garden, Maud', so Maud is the girl of the garden

indicators.note: something given in return comes back, so the word for nothing is read backwards

parts.note: nil means nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A soppy girl in the garden asks for nothing back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in return' turns NIL into LIN. The garden-girl comes from Tennyson's poem 'Maud', with its line 'Come into the garden, Maud'.
explanation.definitionFit: Maudlin describes tearful, gushing emotion, a synonym for sentimental.

clue.text: Is pole in drab housing because of job loss?

indicators.note: the word for drab is housing the other letters, holding them within it

parts.note: drab means dull and dreary, dismal
taken as written
S stands for the south pole

explanation.surface: A question whether a Pole stuck in grim lodgings has lost a job.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing' signals the container; 'pole' looks like a Polish person but is a compass point, the south pole.
explanation.definitionFit: A dismissal is a sacking, the loss of one's employment.

clue.text: Man-servant going to a dance

parts.note: a valet is a gentleman's personal man-servant

explanation.surface: A butler heads off to a ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The valeta is an old-time ballroom dance in waltz time.
explanation.definitionFit: The valeta is a kind of old-time ballroom dance, a waltz variant.

clue.text: Retired engineer still over the moon

indicators.note: retiring means withdrawing or going back, so the engineer's letters are read backwards

parts.note: CE stands for civil engineer
still means motionless, static

explanation.surface: An engineer who has retired remains thrilled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' turns CE (civil engineer) into EC.
explanation.definitionFit: Over the moon is an idiom for being delighted, overjoyed.

clue.text: Agree, anyway, as the priest always appears bellicose

indicators.note: anyway suggests the letters of the word agree can be set down in any order

parts.note: as can mean because, which is for
taken as written
Fr is short for Father, a priest's title
ay (aye) is a poetic word for always, ever

explanation.surface: A priest who always agrees seems keen to fight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anyway' rearranges AGREE into EAGER. AY, or aye, is an old word for always, as in 'for aye'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone eager for the fray is keen to join a fight, which is what bellicose means.

clue.text: Stay on — at least until tomorrow

definitions.text: Stay on — at least until tomorrow

parts.words: Stay on — at least until tomorrow
parts.note: staying somewhere for the night, breaking a journey before moving on the next day

explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads like an instruction to keep working late, but describes a break in a journey for a night.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopover is a short stay, often overnight, in the middle of a journey.

clue.text: Passage to a place offshore

parts.note: an isle is an island, a place out at sea

explanation.surface: A sea voyage out to an island.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats, a passageway.

clue.text: Popular shooting area within striking distance

parts.note: in means fashionable, popular
a range is an area for target shooting

explanation.surface: A busy rifle range lies close enough to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: In range means near enough for a shot or blow to reach, close by.

clue.text: Little Patricia is in a film

parts.note: Pat is a short form of the name Patricia
taken as written

explanation.surface: Young Patricia appears in a movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'film' looks like a cinema film, but here it is a thin surface layer.
explanation.definitionFit: A patina is a thin coating or sheen on a surface, such as on old bronze.

clue.text: Georgia railway loss is in the list of explanations

indicators.note: the word loss is in, placed inside, the letters for Georgia

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia
taken as written

explanation.surface: A railway in Georgia records a loss in its glossary of terms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' signals the container. Georgia here is the US state, not the country, giving its postal code.
explanation.definitionFit: A glossary is an alphabetical list of terms with their meanings explained.

clue.text: A woman admits plot is novel

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: a dame is a woman
a bed is a garden plot, as in flower bed

explanation.surface: A woman confesses that the storyline is fresh.
explanation.walkthrough: 'admits' signals the container. 'novel' looks like an adjective meaning new; it is the book, George Eliot's 1859 novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam Bede is George Eliot's first full-length novel, a work of fiction.

clue.text: Masses of water contained therein

parts.note: huge bodies of sea water, and also lots of water, with the sense of being held within

explanation.walkthrough: The word works two ways: the great seas, and the informal use for a large amount, as in 'loads of water'.
explanation.definitionFit: The great seas of the world are vast bodies of salt water.

clue.text: Sheriff's officer means to reward employees

parts.note: a tip is a gratuity, a means of rewarding service
staff are employees

explanation.surface: A sheriff's man looks for ways to pay his workers bonuses.
explanation.walkthrough: A tipstaff is an officer of a court, named for the metal-tipped staff carried as a badge of office.
explanation.definitionFit: A tipstaff is a court or sheriff's officer, originally carrying a tipped staff.

clue.text: Onlooker who is put in charge

explanation.surface: A spectator gets made the boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The first sense reads the word literally: one who sees things, looking over them.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the word is one who looks on, a spectator; in normal use it is a supervisor or foreman given control.

clue.text: Plan to have little time in Ramsgate, maybe

indicators.note: the small time letter goes in among the letters of the town
maybe suggests the town's name is only one possible arrangement of its letters

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Someone plans to spend a short while in the Kent seaside town of Ramsgate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts T among the letters of RAMSGATE, and 'maybe' rearranges the lot. Ramsgate is a seaside town in Kent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stratagem is a cunning scheme or trick, a plan for gaining an advantage.

clue.text: Hinted at by one legislator with legal support

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the word for legal comes last

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
an MP, Member of Parliament, makes laws
licit means lawful, legal

explanation.surface: Something suggested by a lone MP with legal backing.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue a 'support' sits below what it holds up, so the legal word comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: Implicit means suggested without being said directly, implied.

clue.text: Award given to the top negotiator

parts.note: a diploma is a certificate awarded for a qualification

indicators.note: the top of a word is its first letter, here taken from the word the

explanation.surface: A certificate goes to the best negotiator.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top' looks like 'best', but it takes the first letter of 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A diplomat is an envoy who conducts talks between nations.

clue.text: Awaiting delivery at the supermarket

explanation.surface: Goods are on order, waiting to be stocked at the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means coming in the future, about to happen, and also literally inside a shop.

clue.text: Refuse to deal with ex-Yorkshire cricket captain

explanation.surface: A shunned former leader of the county cricket side.
explanation.walkthrough: Geoffrey Boycott captained Yorkshire, an English county cricket team, and later England.
explanation.definitionFit: To shun a firm or country is to refuse to trade with it; Geoffrey Boycott was a famous Yorkshire and England batsman and captain.

clue.text: Henry put weight on — a great deal

parts.note: Hal is a familiar form of Henry, as with Shakespeare's Prince Hal
to fat is an old verb for fatten, put weight on an animal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Henry piled on the pounds, and a lot of them.
explanation.walkthrough: Prince Hal is Shakespeare's young Henry V. 'Fat' as a verb, as in 'the fatted calf', means fatten.
explanation.definitionFit: Half a ton is an informal exaggeration for a large amount, a lot.

clue.text: Manage to acquire a stylish carriage

parts.note: to land a job or prize is to manage to get it
U means upper-class, socially acceptable and smart

explanation.surface: Someone succeeds in getting hold of an elegant coach.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the old label for upper-class usage, as opposed to non-U, so it stands for posh or stylish.
explanation.definitionFit: A landau is a four-wheeled horse-drawn carriage with a folding top.

clue.text: Also made a lot of waves

parts.note: a swell is a heaving of the sea, a mass of rolling waves

explanation.surface: Someone also caused a great stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made a lot of waves' looks like causing trouble; it is A + SWELL, rolling sea.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means in addition, too, a synonym for also.

clue.text: Escape from Geneva demanded meticulous planning

indicators.note: the letters are taken from within the words Geneva demanded, read as a run

explanation.surface: Breaking out of a Swiss city needed careful planning.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'Geneva demanded'; 'meticulous planning' only finishes the picture of a careful getaway.
explanation.definitionFit: To evade is to escape from or avoid someone or something.

clue.text: Cabaret act makes admirer take to the floor

parts.note: a fan is an admirer
to take to the dance floor is to dance

explanation.surface: A nightclub show inspires an admirer to start dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan dance is a burlesque routine performed behind large feather fans.

clue.text: He fantasises about love-affair with Regina

parts.note: a romance is a love affair
R stands for Regina, Latin for queen, as in royal cyphers

explanation.surface: A dreamer imagines a romance with the queen.
explanation.walkthrough: Regina is Latin for queen; its R appears in royal cyphers such as ER.
explanation.definitionFit: A romancer is one who makes up fanciful stories, a teller of tall tales.

clue.text: Slater gets upset by danger-signals

indicators.note: being upset means being knocked over and disordered, so the name's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man called Slater is unsettled by warning signs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets upset' rearranges SLATER.
explanation.definitionFit: Alerts are warnings, signals that danger is near.

clue.text: Just now have confidence about us currency

indicators.note: about means around, so the trust word goes around the coin

parts.note: to rely on is to have confidence in
the cent is a unit of US currency

explanation.surface: Lately people have trusted the American dollar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' signals the container. 'us' looks like the pronoun; it is US, the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Recently means lately, a short time ago.
